goal: Add an honest self-generated synthetic test-video capability to the completed CS Demo Integrity project, verify it with real FFmpeg/FFprobe media evidence, and rebuild the canonical package through local_packager.
acceptance_criteria: make-test-video creates WebM or MP4 from a deterministic internal scenario without a downloaded demo.
The video shows player positions, subject aim, target relation, visibility or information state, shots, and progress.
The video and manifest visibly and structurally state that it is synthetic evidence visualization, not gameplay and not a cheating verdict.
External JSON or .dem input requires an authorization assertion and uses the same normalized model.
FFmpeg encoding and FFprobe validation produce a hashed sidecar manifest; missing tooling fails honestly.
Generated-project tests, actual video generation, canonical evidence, package inspection, and applicable CGKN regression pass.

quality_metrics.target: valid probed media plus sidecar hash and synthetic disclaimer
quality_metrics.method: pytest, CLI run, FFprobe, manifest inspection

quality_metrics.target: local_packager remains the only packaging exit and no Telegram generation route changes
quality_metrics.method: kernel contract tests and canonical manifest inspection

prevention: Keep the renderer inside the generated project's typed normalized model and label all synthetic output.
assurance: Review authorization, no-gameplay-claim, dependency, and delivery-boundary behavior.
control: Run unit tests, actual FFmpeg integration, FFprobe inspection, canonical test/runtime/visual evidence, and package inspection.
improvement: Record whether direct raw-frame streaming avoids temporary-frame growth while remaining portable.

interface_expectations.contract: make-test-video accepts optional authorized input and returns a hashed SyntheticTestVideoManifest
NormalizedMatch ticks provide positions, view angles, shots, visibility, and information state

feedback: The project generated its own 8-second 960x540 VP9 test video with 160 frames, visible synthetic disclaimer, moving player and aim relationships, FFprobe PASS, and a matching SHA-256 sidecar.
All 58 reviewed project tests, isolated runtime, browser visual evidence, complexity contract, canonical package, media validation, and applicable CGKN management/kernel tests passed.
Real production .dem compatibility, calibrated detection rates, and Telegram production provenance remain outside this bounded increment.

worked: A single vertical increment added scenario generation, typed rendering, CLI, documentation, tests, real media, and a rebuilt package without changing CGKN generation or delivery routes.
Streaming RGB frames directly to FFmpeg avoided temporary-frame growth and produced a valid 8-second VP9 video.
The same NormalizedMatch contract supports generated synthetic input, authorized JSON, and optional authorized .dem parsing.
did_not_work: The first media test exposed a broken pre-existing Pillow installation that advertised version 10.4.0 but lacked PIL._deprecate; reinstalling the declared dependency restored the environment.
Naming the exception TestVideoError caused pytest to consider it a test class; renaming it VideoBuildError removed the collection warning.
experiments: Stream Pillow RGB frames directly to FFmpeg stdin so the project creates a useful video without storing hundreds of temporary images.
